reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read Jesus's remark as a complaint that the disciples stopped pressing the question, not a denial that Peter and Thomas had ever asked it.

discrepancy.connective: Raymond E. Brown reads 16:5 as a seam: written without 13:36 or 14:5 in view, evidence the Farewell Discourse stitches together separate source material.

skeptic.name: Raymond E. Brown
skeptic.work: The Gospel According to John XIII-XXI, Anchor Bible 29A
skeptic.attribution: Raymond E. Brown, The Gospel According to John XIII-XXI, Anchor Bible 29A (Doubleday, 1970), pp. 581-604, 710

excerpts.excerpt_text: They had done so in a sort (Joh 13:36; Joh 14:5); but He wished more intelligent and eager inquiry on the subject.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: JFB explicitly names both antecedent questions (13:36, 14:5) and reconciles 16:5 by reframing it as a complaint about insufficient follow-up, not a denial that they had spoken up at all.

pd_work.note: John Haley's Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible was checked (curl+grep of the full djvu text for 'whither goest', 'goest thou', 'none of you', 'asketh', 'xvi. 5', 'xiii. 36', 'xiv. 5') and shows no coverage of this specific Farewell Discourse question-and-denial crux. Falling back to JFB's own note on John 16:5, already surfaced on this row, which treats the passage directly and names both antecedent verses.
